preamble: Fortition and devoicing of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] (Arabic ghayn) to the voiceless uvular stop [q]. It is reported sporadically in Gulf Arabic, where ghayn occasionally surfaces as [q], a development attributed to Persian influence (Persian merged ghayn and qaf). The better-known Ḥassāniyya case, where geminate ghayn is realized [qː], involves a uvular [ʁ] and belongs under ʁ → q.

examples.note: Ghayn occasionally changes to [q] (or /ɡ/), attributed to Persian influence; the change is sporadic and lexically restricted (Qafisheh 1977: 266).

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Gulf Arabic (Consonants; citing Qafisheh 1977, A Short Reference Grammar of Gulf Arabic, p. 266). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Arabic
